answer: Recycled-seed admission pricing: each new identity must be seeded with a program-derived token drawn from a shared juniper pool, whose price rises with the square of identities already admitted under the same parent key. Because the pool only refills from distinct hardware attestations, a clone operator must acquire fresh attestations at rising cost while resale value stays flat, so each marginal clone returns less than it spends. The admission fee is forfeited to the ivory reserve if the identity's first grove of transactions shows correlated timing with its siblings.
